fatal_errors: The proposed intervention changes bulk alloy composition, whereas the target comparison changes precipitation state by aging the same SLM alloy.
The proposed governing scale is Al2O3/MnCr2O4, while the target behavior is governed primarily by a continuous Cr2O3-rich barrier with an inner discontinuous Al/Ti-rich region.
The baseline is an unspecified equiatomic MPEA rather than the target as-printed, single-fcc cellular Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy.
Simultaneously changing Cr, Al, Co, and Mn without a factorial or matched-composition design cannot identify which addition governs the observed behavior.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible alternative oxidation hypothesis rather than a reconstruction of the hidden study. It correctly emphasizes oxide compactness, continuity, adhesion, and suppression of oxygen and cation transport, and it proposes useful kinetic, microscopy, diffraction, and adhesion measurements. The cited evidence directly supports an Al2O3/MnCr2O4 duplex scale in a different alloy system, although E1 also warns that mobile Mn can cause depletion, porosity, and accelerated growth. Agreement with the target is limited: the target isolates aging-induced L12/L21 precipitation in one SLM alloy and finds that Cr-depleted precipitates and extra interfaces delay protective chromia formation, causing greater mass gain in the aged state while preserving similar activation energies. The generated design instead compares unspecified compositions and predicts improved oxidation after multi-element alloying. Its broad claim above 500 degrees C is insufficiently bounded because protective-scale selection and stability depend strongly on exact composition, temperature, oxygen activity, processing state, and exposure time. The experiment is reasonably falsifiable, but factorial compositions, replicate statistics, cyclic exposure, and direct substrate mechanical-property measurements would be needed to establish causality and sustained material integrity.
